KB BEST Payment Files

Domestic transfers, direct debits and foreign/SEPA payments from a Komerční banka account, exported in KB's BEST format from an OCA payment order.

Version19.0.1.1.0
EditionCommunity and Enterprise
LicenceAGPL-3
Requiresaccount_payment_order, account_kb_best_base, base_iban

What it is for

BEST is Komerční banka's own fixed-width client format for its direct banking channels — MojeBanka Business, Profibanka and Přímý kanál (direct channel). This module writes BEST payment files from an OCA payment order (account_payment_order), so you pay a batch of bills from your KB account by uploading one file. It works on Community and Enterprise alike.

The specification is KB's Klientský formát BEST podporovaný v KB, valid from 20 June 2026.

Statements in the same format are imported by account_statement_import_kb_best.

Payment methods

Payment method Payment order BEST record File
KB BEST (domestic transfer) outbound (Payment Orders) 01, domestic transfer BEST-DP-<journal>-<date and time>.ikm
KB BEST (domestic direct debit / inkaso) inbound (Debit Orders) 01 with the direct-debit operation code BEST-DP-….ikm
KB BEST (foreign / SEPA transfer) outbound 02 with the 03 structured address BEST-ZP-<journal>-<date and time>.ikm

Files are Windows-1250 with CR LF line ends; domestic records keep Czech diacritics, foreign records use only the SWIFT character set.

Setting it up

  1. The bank journal (Accounting → Configuration → Accounting → Journals) must hold a KB account — bank code 0100 — as a CZ IBAN or prefix-number/0100. Any other account is refused. The journal's currency (or the company's, if the journal has none) is taken as the currency of the KB account.
  2. A payment mode for each method you use (Accounting → Configuration → Accounting → Payment Modes), with the KB journal.
  3. Partners: a bank account for everyone you pay. For a foreign payment that is not SEPA also the partner's street, city and country, and the BIC of their bank (or the bank's name, city and country).
  4. Recommended: l10n_cssk_payment_symbols so that each bill's symbols reach the payment lines on their own (see account_abo).

Making a payment file

  1. Accounting → Vendors → Payment Orders (or Customers → Debit Orders for direct debits), New, choose the KB BEST payment mode, Create Payment Lines from Journal Items.
  2. Check Variable Symbol, Constant Symbol and Specific Symbol on the lines; an empty one is taken from a VS: / KS: / SS: token in the Communication.
  3. Confirm Payments, Generate Payment File.
  4. Upload the .ikm file in MojeBanka Business, Profibanka or Přímý kanál, authorise it there, and mark the order with File Successfully Uploaded.

Rules the file follows

These are KB's rules; the module applies them before the bank does and stops with a message naming the payment:

Every payment

  • the amount must be positive;
  • a due date in the past is moved to today (the bank refuses a past one);
  • each payment gets a sequence number derived from its payment line, because KB requires the number to be unique for the whole day across all files, not only within one file.

Domestic (record 01)

  • the beneficiary's account must be Czech (IBAN CZ… or prefix-number/bank code);
  • a payment in another currency than the KB account's is sent with KB's conversion flag; a non-CZK domestic payment may only go to another KB account — to any other bank it must be in CZK or sent as a foreign payment;
  • a direct debit from another bank than KB must be in CZK;
  • constant symbols KB refuses in a batch are refused here too: ???5 (corrective settlement), ??51 (enforcement), 0006 and 0007;
  • the Communication becomes up to four lines of 35 characters of message for the beneficiary, and its first 30 characters your own description;
  • your own VS and SS are sent empty: the bank replaces them with the beneficiary's anyway.

Foreign (record 02)

  • a payment goes as SEPA when it is in EUR, to an IBAN in a SEPA country, with shared charges; everything else is a standard foreign payment;
  • into the EEA only shared charges (SHA) are allowed;
  • a EUR payment into the EEA needs the beneficiary's IBAN;
  • a non-SEPA payment needs the beneficiary's name, street, city and country, and the beneficiary bank's BIC or its name, city and country;
  • the VS and KS are written into the payment details as /VS/… and /KS/…, where KB reads them back into the transaction history;
  • the 03 structured address is added when the partner has a city and a country.

The shared BEST module

The BEST layouts — both payment records and the statement — live in account_kb_best_base, which this module and account_statement_import_kb_best build on. It has no screen of its own.

Limitations

  • Only from a KB account; this is KB's own format.
  • Community payment orders only — there is no Enterprise batch-payment variant of this module.
  • Urgency and charges are set per payment line: Priority (Urgent is KB's express processing) and Charge Bearer (Shared, Payer = OUR, Beneficiary = BEN). They default to normal and shared; into the EEA only Shared is accepted (see above).
  • The order stops at the first payment that breaks a rule; fix it and generate again.
  • KB's XML format for SEPA payments is a separate module, account_payment_kb_sepa.
